identity.name: Government General of Warsaw
alt_names: German occupation zone of Congress Poland

land.text: 'the north-western half of the former Russian-ruled Congress Poland': Warsaw, Lodz, Plock and Kalisz, without the south and the Lublin area held by Austria-Hungary

predecessors.note: Congress Poland ended with the Russian withdrawal of 19 September 1915 (congress-poland ledger). The Warsaw page: the territory 'first formed part of the Ober Ost military command, then came under a separate administration in October'. The congress-poland dossier lists this slug as its successor and books a loss of the Kingdom without Lublin to german-empire.

land.text: 'the north-western half of the former Russian-ruled Congress Poland': Warsaw, Lodz, Plock and Kalisz, without the south and the Lublin area held by Austria-Hungary

successors.note: The Regency Kingdom of Poland (proclaimed 5 November 1916 on this territory and the Austro-Hungarian zone) passed its authority to Pilsudski on 14 November 1918; the Second Polish Republic dossier starts on 11 November 1918.

capitals.name: Warsaw
capitals.note: 'The headquarters of the General Government operated in the Royal Castle, Warsaw'; the governor-general's seat was the Belvedere palace. Coordinates are Warsaw's, approximate.

rulers.name: Hans Hartwig von Beseler
rulers.title: governor-general
rulers.note: 'held his office for the entire duration of the region's existence' (no appointment date on the page). The chiefs of the administration were Wolfgang von Kries (18 October 1915 to 26 November 1917) and Otto von Steinmeister (26 November 1917 to 6 October 1918).

correction.text: 'It encompassed the north-western half of the former Russian-ruled Congress Poland': Warsaw, Lodz, Plock and Kalisz districts, the Lublin and Kielce south being the Austro-Hungarian zone

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (Cliopatria draws all of Congress Poland as German Empire from 1916, the German Empire row of 1,004 new cells in 1915-1916, and nothing for 1915 itself). The page gives no district list, no boundary with the Austro-Hungarian zone and no area; the region is the Duchy of Warsaw 1812 shape less Greater Poland, Krakow, the Chelm governorate and the Lublin and Swietokrzyskie voivodeships (the Austro-Hungarian Military Government of Lublin's 'southern parts of Russian Poland', whose Kielce seat was formed on 25 August 1915), kept to Masovia, Lodz and the Kalisz and Wloclawek districts: 249 cells, about 63,000 km2, roughly half of Congress Poland as the page's 'north-western half' says. Radom, which the Austro-Hungarians held, falls inside Masovia here; unverified.

region.text: 'the north-western half of the former Russian-ruled Congress Poland': Warsaw, Lodz, Plock and Kalisz, without the south and the Lublin area held by Austria-Hungary

ledger.note: October 1915: the Germans set up the Government General of Warsaw over the north-western half of Congress Poland. 'It encompassed the north-western half of the former Russian-ruled Congress Poland'; the territory 'first formed part of the Ober Ost military command, then came under a separate administration in October', the chief of administration Wolfgang von Kries taking office on 18 October 1915; Hans von Beseler was governor-general 'for the entire duration'. The Russians left on 19 September 1915 (congress-poland ledger). The page gives the half, not the districts: the region is the researcher's reading.

region.text: the Kingdom of Poland proclaimed on the territory held as the Government General of Warsaw

ledger.note: 5 November 1916: Germany and Austria-Hungary proclaim the Kingdom of Poland on the occupied land. The Kingdom 'was proclaimed during World War I by it and Austria-Hungary on 5 November 1916' on 'the territories of formerly Russian-ruled Congress Poland held by the Central Powers as the Government General of Warsaw'; Governor Beseler at Warsaw issued the Act of 5th November; the Kingdom became active on 14 January 1917 (Provisional Council of State, 15 members chosen by the Germans and ten by the Austrians) and the Regency Council was installed on 15 October 1917. The Warsaw page: the General Government 'continued to exist alongside it' (the joint administration of both zones had been introduced on 18 October 1916). The Kingdom has no dossier; its vassal tint needs one.

region.text: the Regency Kingdom of Poland, which declared independence on 7 October 1918

ledger.note: 6-7 October 1918: the Germans hand over the administration and the Regency Council declares independence. 'On 6 October, he handed over the administration to Polish civil servants. The Regency Council declared independence on 7 October 1918.' German troops stayed in Warsaw until the armistice.

region.text: 'the north-western half of the former Russian-ruled Congress Poland': Warsaw, Lodz, Plock and Kalisz, without the south and the Lublin area held by Austria-Hungary

ledger.note: 11 November 1918: the German occupation ends with the armistice and Poland is reborn. The Warsaw page's infobox ends the General Government with the 'Armistice, withdrawal of German forces' (no day given); the Kingdom page: German troops in Warsaw 'were disarmed as they refused to fire on Polish insurgents', Pilsudski 'arrived on 10 November' (the armistice was signed the day after), and 'On 14 November, the Council ceded the remainder of its authority to Jozef Pilsudski and voted itself out of existence'.

certainty.note: The pages give no district list and no line between the German and Austro-Hungarian zones ('To the south lay the Austro-Hungarian-controlled Military Government of Lublin'); the region is the researcher's reading of 'the north-western half'.

sources.title: General Government of Warsaw
sources.note: Identity, October 1915 start (Kries from 18 October 1915), 'the north-western half of the former Russian-ruled Congress Poland', Beseler, seat in the Royal Castle, the 18 October 1916 joint administration, chiefs of administration, the Kingdom 'alongside'. No district list, area, appointment date or end date.

sources.title: Military Government of Lublin
sources.note: The Austro-Hungarian neighbour: formed 25 August 1915 as the General Government of Kielce, renamed Lublin on 1 October 1915; 'the southern parts of Russian Poland'; joint administration 18 October 1916; proclamation of the Kingdom on 5 November 1916. No governor, boundary or area.

sources.title: Regency Kingdom of Poland
sources.note: 5 November 1916 proclamation on the territory of the Government General of Warsaw, 14 January 1917 activation, 15 October 1917 Regency Council, 6-7 October 1918 handover and independence, 10-14 November 1918 end.

notes: Requested by the p1910-p1919 window (the land is unowned in 1916-1917 and Russian at the end of 1915). The dossier covers the German Government General of Warsaw only (October 1915 to November 1918), type colony of german-empire (a dependency ruled from Berlin; no vassal_start for it exists in the german-empire ledger, which books the same land as an occupation of the Russian Empire in 1915 and of the Russian Republic from March 1917: those events and this dossier overlap, and the compiler should draw this slug and let the German occupation entries stand for the Ober Ost lands only). Its two companions have no dossier: (1) the Austro-Hungarian Military Government of Lublin, 25 August 1915 (as the General Government of Kielce) to November 1918, seat Lublin, 'the southern parts of Russian Poland' (the austria-hungary ledger books an occupation of congress-poland, Lublin and Swietokrzyskie, 1 September 1915 to November 1918; the congress-poland successors list it as military-government-of-lublin); (2) the Regency Kingdom of Poland, 5 November 1916 to 14 November 1918, a Central Powers client over both zones, which this ledger tints as a vassal of this government (the vassal counterpart is the kingdom itself) and for which a dossier is needed so the tint has a state. Alternative the window suggested (an occupation relation in the congress-poland ledger instead of a loss to german-empire) is not taken: the congress-poland dossier already names this slug as successor. Not settled: the districts (Radom, Suwalki, Lomza, Plock, Kalisz) and the line to the Austro-Hungarian zone; the existing congress-poland and austria-hungary regions overlap on Swietokrzyskie; this dossier follows the Austro-Hungarian side; Cliopatria's Duchy of Warsaw 1812 shape reaches 15.5 E in the west and 49.8 N in the south, beyond Congress Poland, so the region is intersected with Masovia, Lodz and two discs. Wars: none listed; the Great Retreat of 1915 is in the congress-poland, russian-empire and german-empire ledgers and no page opened for this dossier describes it. Gazetteer names needed: Wloclawek (place; the region uses a coordinate disc at 19.07 E 52.65 N, from the researcher's knowledge, not a page), Plock, Lomza. Wikidata id not known.
